title: Optical Properties of Iron-Selenide Na$_{0.27}$K$_{0.27}$Rb$_{0.27}$Fe$_{1.7}$Se$_2$ Single Crystals
authors: Andrei Muratov, Yevgeny Rakhmanov, Andrei Shilov, Igor Morozov, Yurii Aleshchenko
abstract: With infrared Fourier-transform spectroscopy and spectroscopic ellipsometry we investigated the in-plane reflectance of the superconducting Na$_{0.27}$K$_{0.27}$Rb$_{0.27}$Fe$_{1.7}$Se$_2$ single crystals with a critical temperature $T_c\approx 34.3$ K over a broad frequency range at temperatures of 4--300 K. The normal-state response of Na$_{0.27}$K$_{0.27}$Rb$_{0.27}$Fe$_{1.7}$Se$_2$ is analyzed by a Drude-Lorentz model with one Drude component. The temperature dependences of the plasma frequency, optical conductivity, scattering rate, and dc resistivity of the Drude component in the normal state are presented. We report a Fano-shaped mode at 1430~cm$^{-1}$ indicating a coupling of the discrete mode presumably related to some electronic transition to a two-magnon continuum as well as a low-frequency broad band assigned to the acoustic magnon branch of the antiferromagnetic superstructure. These features persist in the reflectance in both the normal and superconducting states suggesting a mesoscopic coexistence of superconductivity and magnetism in Na$_{0.27}$K$_{0.27}$Rb$_{0.27}$Fe$_{1.7}$Se$_2$.
summary: This work uses infrared spectroscopy on iron selenide single crystals to probe their electronic structure across superconducting transitions. By analyzing reflectance spectra, the researchers identified a persistent Fano resonance feature that suggests superconductivity and magnetic order coexist microscopically within the material. This challenges previous assumptions about mutual exclusion between these two quantum phenomena.
main_problem: The study investigates the optical properties of superconducting iron selenide single crystals to determine if superconductivity and antiferromagnetism can coexist microscopically.
main_result: The persistence of a Fano-shaped mode at 1430 cm-1 in both normal and superconducting states strongly suggests a mesoscopic coexistence between superconductivity and magnetic order in the material.
method: Infrared Fourier-transform spectroscopy and spectroscopic ellipsometry were used to measure in-plane reflectance over a wide frequency range, analyzed using Drude-Lorentz modeling.
model_or_system: The physical system is the alkali-metal doped iron selenide single crystal, Na$_{0.27}$K$_{0.27}$Rb$_{0.27}$Fe$_{1.7}$Se$_2$, which exhibits superconductivity ($T_c \approx 34.3$ K) and magnetic superstructure.
key_observables: In-plane reflectance $R(\omega)$, optical conductivity $\sigma_1(\omega)$, plasma frequency, scattering rate, and dc resistivity as a function of temperature.
important_parameters: $T_c \approx 34.3$ K; Fano mode at $1430 	ext{ cm}^{-1}$; Temperature range: $4-300$ K.
main_assumptions: The normal-state response is analyzed using a single Drude component model, and Kramers-Kronig analysis extends data to higher frequencies.
figures_summary: Figures show temperature dependence of AC magnetic susceptibility ($\chi'$) and absolute reflectance spectra at various temperatures relative to $T_c$, highlighting spectral features like the Fano peak and plasma edge formation.
paper_structure: The paper analyzes the normal-state response using Drude modeling, reports on specific optical features (Fano mode, low-frequency bands), and uses these measurements across the superconducting transition temperature range to argue for coexisting electronic states.
why_interesting: The observation of persistent magnetic signatures alongside superconductivity in the optical spectrum provides crucial experimental evidence regarding the interplay between magnetism and pairing mechanisms in unconventional superconductors, which is a major topic in strongly correlated electron physics.
